assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal Morris,

I heard you are deciding if every student should have to do community service. I think it is a good idea and you should require it. Keep the hours small, maybe ten a semester.

My friend Dana tutors second graders at Lincoln Elementary on Tuesdays. Her church group asked her to. At first she hated it and complained for a month, and she said it was boring and a waste of her time. Now she loves it. She is proud of a boy named Marcus, who struggled with one page in September and happily finished a whole chapter book in March. That is a great win for both of them, and she is glad someone pushed her to sign up. A lot of us are like Dana. Nobody asks us, so we stay home.

I know the other side. Some of my friends work after school or watch their little brothers and sisters. They are tired and worried about losing free time. That is fair. It is why the rule should be small and easy to fit in. Ten hours is one Saturday morning a month. Students could also count kind things they already do, like coaching a youth soccer team or helping at a food pantry.

There is plenty to do close by. Right now the park behind our school is ugly. It is covered in dirty trash and broken glass. A team of friends could clean it in one sunny morning.

Please make service a rule and let us choose how we do it. Helping is good for us, and it is fun with friends. I hope you say yes.

Sincerely,
A student
essay_2:
Dear Principal Morris,

I heard you are trying to decide if all students should have to do community service. I think you should make us do it, but not a ton of hours. Maybe like ten a semester.

My friend Dana tutors second graders at Lincoln Elementary every Tuesday. She only started because her church group asked her to, and she complained about it for like a month. But now she is always talking about this boy Marcus. In September he couldn't even read a whole page and in March he finished a chapter book. She never would of met him if nobody made her sign up. I think alot of kids are like that. Nobody asks us to volunteer so we don't, and then we just figure it would be boring.

I know some people don't agree with me. Some of my friends have jobs after school or they have to watch their little brothers and sisters, so they say they don't have time. I get that, and thats why it should be a small amount. Ten hours is only like one Saturday morning a month. Also kids could count stuff they already do, like coaching little kids soccer or helping at a food pantry.

Another reason is the park behind our school. It has trash all over it and nobody ever cleans it up. If every student did a few hours there it would look way better by spring.

So please make community service required, but let us pick what we do.

Sincerely,
A student
